title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Marya – Mariah – Madya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Yonah, as in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra, chapter 8, end of halakhah 1, where he brought a case before Rabbi Yose; in Ketubot 9:1 he asked before Rabbi Yonah; in Shabbat 14:4 he spoke in Rabbi Yonah’s name, and likewise in Sanhedrin 1:2; and at the end of Eruvin, chapter 8, he said to Rabbi Mana: “Thus said Rabbi Yonah, your father.” In Sheviit, chapter 6, end of halakhah 1, Rabbi Chiyya bar Madya said to Rabbi Mana: “You did well not to sign (the permission), for Rabbi Yonah your father said,” etc. In Pesikta deRav Kahana, historical folio 153b, we find Rabbi Chiyya bar Madya in the name of Rabbi Levi.

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah series is Jerusalem Talmud. “Your father” explicitly refers to Rabbi Yonah as Mana’s father, not to Rabbi Chiyya’s father. Pesikta folio 153b remains historical pagination without an unproved modern section conversion.

Guggenheimer Sheviit 6:1 directly has Chiyya bar Madya approving Mana’s refusal to sign and citing “Rabbi Yonah your father.” The other Marya/Mariah occurrences and historical Pesikta 153b citation remain separate locators, not established equivalences from this one passage.
